content.summary_of_the_paper: Based on previous Online Continual Object Detection in video, this paper introduces a new setting called Label-Efficient Online Continual Object Detection (LEOCOD) via using fewer annotations and learning in an online manner.  This paper presents Efficient-CLS, a plug-and-play module that can be easily inserted into and improve existing continual learners.  It contains two feed-forward neural networks as slow and fast learners. The weights of the slow learner change a little on each reinstatement, and are maintained by taking the exponential moving average (EMA) of the fast learner’s weights over time. Results on OAK and EgoObjects shows the effectiveness of proposed approaches.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 

1, The writing is good and easy to follow. 

2, The proposed new settings are interesting and new to my knowledge. Using fewer annotations for video object detection is interesting. 

3, The proposed Efficient-CLS, shows the effectiveness over stronger baseline in Tab.1 for two different datasets. 

Weakness.

1, The proposed solution Efficient-CLS seems to be not new. I am not expert for continual learning. However, the faster-slow (teacher-student) frames with EMA update are very common for domain adaption and domain generation, also common in semi-supervised detection and segmentation.  Thus, the novelty is limited. 

2, Several details: How to sample the key annotations? How about both side using the slow or faster learners?

3, The proposed approach does not consider the temporal consistency. 

4, Several related works on Video Object Detection are missing:

1. Flow-guided feature aggregation for video object detection
2. Deep feature flow for video recognition.
3. Transvod: End-to-end video object detection with spatial-temporal transformers
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Clarity, Quality are good. For Novelty, I am not sure about such framework in this cases.
content.summary_of_the_review: Combine these, I rate this paper as board line. I am not sure the real technique novelty of fast-slow learner for Continual Learning. I am sure it is not new for such solution.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a method for online continual object detection. It focuses on the real life streaming setting where new incoming data may have some distribution shift and each data point is only seen once during the whole training process. The proposed method consists of a fast learner trained by supervised labels and pseudo labels, and a slow learner, whose weights are the running average of the fast learner, to provide pseudo labels. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method perform better than the baseline method by a clear margin.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength
1. The setting studied here has the potential to apply to various real-life applications.
2. Writing is clear and easy to follow.
3. Experiments show consistent improvement from the baseline method.

## Weaknesses
My major concern is about novelty. The proposed method seems a direct application of [1]. In both this paper and [1], the slow learner's weights are the running average of that of the fast learner, and the training target of the fast learner is provided by the slow learner. The only change is that in [1] the loss function is contrastive loss while this paper has object detection loss. In the meantime, [1] was not cited in this paper.


[1] He, Kaiming, et al. "Momentum contrast for unsupervised visual representation learning." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF conference on computer vision and pattern recognition. 2020.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall the studied setting is interesting and of much practical importance, while the proposed method seems almost the same as the MoCo paper [1], which makes the novelty unclear.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents an online continual learning approach from a continuous video stream for object detection in streaming video. Particularly, a plug-and-play module is introduced to learn from a mini-batch containing a set of consecutive video frames where only a fixed proportion of frames are labeled. The module consists of two feed-forward neural networks:  a fast learner network that rapidly adapted to the current detection task, and a slow learner that changes a little on each reinstatement and generates pseudo labels for unannotated frames in the mini-batch. In experiments, the proposed approach was evaluated on benchmark datasets OAK and EgoObjects.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 

- Develops a plug-and-play online continual learning module consisting of two feedforward networks for the task of object detection in streaming video.

- Designs a complimentary system for online continual learning: (i) a fast learner is designed to quickly encode new knowledge from the current data stream and then consolidate it to the slow learner; and (ii) a slow learner accumulates the acquired knowledge from the fast learner over time and guides the fast learner.

Weaknesses

- The label-efficiency of the proposed approach seems limited. The proposed approach (with 25% annotations) is able to surpass the best baseline which was trained at 100%. But the performance will be drastically dropped at a lower annotation cost than 25%. For video annotations, a 4x reduction in annotation cost seems limited. 

- The generalization ability of the proposed module seems limited. The proposed CLS module only improves over a part of state-of-the-art methods, as reflected in Table 1. Particularly, the improvements in FAP on OAK over methods A-GEM and DER++ are marginal. Also, the F score on EgoObjects with CLS actually dropped rather than improved. It would be better to include detailed ablations and clarifications on the metrics.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The author(s) promised to release the code in the future for reproducibility but a link to the implementation is not included in the paper.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper presents a simple and sensible complementary plug-and-play module for online continual learning for object detection in streaming video which learns from a continuous video stream with partial annotations. But the annotation cost reduction ability and the generalization ability of the proposed module seem limited.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper works on a new problem setting of online continue learning for object detection in streaming video: given a stream of videos where parts on the frames are labeled, the models is required to infer on unlabeled frames. The models are also tested on earlier frames to ensure they are not forgetting knowledges during online learning. The authors proposed a teacher-student learning framework based on EMA pseudo-labels. The proposed framework significantly outperforms baselines on this new tasks, and can match the baselines with only 25% data.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

+ The paper works on a new and interesting problem setting which is closer to human visual perception. The proposed method can be a good baseline on this direction.

+ The results are strong as shown in Figure 1 and Table 1. The proposed method outperform the baseline (Wang et al.) by a healthy margin, and the authors show their method works under different frameworks (Table 1).

+ The paper is well written and easy to understand. Figure 1 nicely illustrated the target of the work and highlighted the results. Figure 2 clearly shows the proposed method.

Weaknesses

- As this is a new task, it is unclear for me how hard the problem is. The authors already include a good number of baselines to compare to, however it's still not 100% convincing, especially given that the detector used in the baseline is trained on Pascal VOC (Sec 4.4). More discussion on the baselines might address this concern.

- The authors used a pre-defined train-test split from the dataset (to compare with existing works). It would also be interesting to see how the split affects the difficulty of the task: e.g., can we use one day of data as training as the next day as testing? Note this is NOT required in the rebuttal.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clear, in good quality, and novel. The code is not mentioned, and it might be hard to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper works on an interesting new problem with a reasonable framework and good results. I didn't find significant drawbacks, and recommend a borderline accept for now. However I have little knowledge on this problem and might change my rating when seeing other reviews.
